title: Linux Security Hardening: Lynis Scores Across Different Distributions
description: This content discusses the use of Lynis, a security auditing and hardening tool for Linux and UNIX-based systems, to evaluate the security posture of various Linux distributions using their default configurations. It presents a comparative overview of Lynis Hardening Index scores across multiple distributions, indicating the relative security measures in place by default. The information is intended as a basic comparison and not a definitive security assessment.

aiSummary: Lynis is an open-source security auditing tool designed for UNIX-like systems, including Linux and macOS. It performs in-depth security scans to assess system defenses, compliance with standards (e.g., HIPAA, ISO27001, PCI DSS), and provides recommendations for system hardening. The provided data shows Lynis Hardening Index scores for different Linux distributions tested with default settings using Lynis version 3.1.7. Higher scores indicate more security measures are enabled by default. This comparison highlights the varying levels of default security hardening across distributions but does not represent a vulnerability or exploit.
aiImpact: There is no direct security vulnerability or exploit described. The impact is informational, showing that some Linux distributions have stronger default security configurations than others. This can guide system administrators in choosing distributions or understanding the baseline security posture before further hardening.
